q: The legendary 'Orient Express' train service of Europe famously ran between:
e: The legendary Orient Express famously ran between Paris and Istanbul, becoming the most celebrated luxury train service of Europe.

q: 'Maglev' trains, which run without touching the rails, work on the principle of:
e: Maglev trains work on magnetic levitation: powerful magnets lift and propel the train, so it floats above the guideway without touching the rails.

q: The Qinghai-Tibet railway, the highest railway line in the world, is located in:
e: The Qinghai-Tibet railway in China is the highest railway line in the world, crossing the Tanggula Pass at over 5,000 metres above sea level.

q: In railway track, 'cant' (superelevation) refers to:

options.A: The raising of the outer rail above the inner rail on a curve
options.B: The distance between the two rails of a track
options.C: The gap left between two rail joints
options.D: The slope of the railway embankment

e: Cant or superelevation is the raising of the outer rail above the inner rail on a curve, so that trains can safely negotiate the curve at speed.

q: In the 'EOG' (End On Generation) system of train lighting and air-conditioning:

options.A: Power is drawn from the locomotive through head-on generation
options.B: Batteries under the coaches supply all the power
options.C: Diesel generator power cars attached at the ends of the rake supply power to the coaches
options.D: Solar panels on coach roofs supply the power

e: In the End On Generation system, diesel generator power cars attached at one or both ends of the rake supply electricity for coach lighting and air-conditioning.

q: Under the token system of working on single-line sections, the token carried by the driver serves as:

options.A: A permit to exceed the speed limit
options.B: The authority for the train to enter and run through the block section
options.C: A receipt for the goods carried in the train
options.D: An identification badge of the driver

e: Under the token system on single-line sections, the token carried by the driver is itself the authority for the train to enter and occupy the block section.

q: 'BOXN' wagons of Indian Railways are:

options.D: Open bogie wagons used mainly for carrying coal and other bulk commodities

e: BOXN wagons are open bogie wagons of Indian Railways used mainly for carrying coal and other bulk commodities such as ores.

q: The trains of the Kolkata Metro draw power from:

options.A: A third rail at 750 volt DC
options.C: A third rail at 1,500 volt DC

e: The Kolkata Metro, India's first metro, draws power from a third rail supplied at 750 volt DC.

q: Under the Automatic Block System of signalling:

options.A: Only one train can be present in the entire section between two stations
options.B: The driver himself operates all the signals on the route
options.C: The section is divided into several sub-sections and the signals work automatically according to the position of trains
options.D: Trains are worked by written authority throughout

e: Under the Automatic Block System, the section is divided into several sub-sections and signals are worked automatically by the movement and position of trains, allowing closer headways.

q:
Consider the following statements about India's first passenger train of 1853:
1. It carried about 400 passengers.
2. It consisted of 14 carriages.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. India's first passenger train of 16 April 1853, running from Bori Bunder to Thane, carried about 400 passengers in 14 carriages.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Matheran Light Railway is a narrow gauge line.
2. The Kangra Valley Railway is a metre gauge line.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: the Matheran Light Railway is a narrow gauge line. Statement 2 is false: the Kangra Valley Railway is also narrow gauge (762 mm), not metre gauge.

q: The number of tunnels on the Kalka-Shimla Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage line, is about:
e: The Kalka-Shimla Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage mountain line, passes through about 102 tunnels on its 96 km route.

q: Dimapur, the principal railway station and railhead of its State, is located in:
e: Dimapur is the principal railway station and railhead of Nagaland, the State's main link with the rest of the country by rail.

q: 'Namma Metro' is the metro rail system of the city of:
e: Namma Metro, which literally means 'our metro', is the metro rail system of Bengaluru.

q: The air brake system used in trains was invented by:
e: The air brake system used in trains was invented by George Westinghouse, whose compressed-air brakes greatly improved railway safety.

q: The phrase 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: The expression 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 has been borrowed from the Constitution of Japan.

q: The President of India nominates how many members to the Rajya Sabha from amongst persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art and social service?
e: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from among persons with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

q: Under the Constitution of India, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the:
e: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, which can remove it through a no-confidence motion.

q: The word 'Cabinet' was inserted in the Constitution of India (in Article 352) by the:
e: The word 'Cabinet' was inserted in Article 352 of the Constitution by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

q: The idea of a Constituent Assembly for framing the Constitution of India was first put forward by:
e: The idea of a Constituent Assembly to frame India's Constitution was first put forward by M. N. Roy in 1934.

q: The highest law officer of a State Government in India is the:

options.C: Chief Justice of the High Court

e: The Advocate General is the highest law officer of a State Government, corresponding at the State level to the Attorney General for India.

q: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) is associated with the recommendation for the establishment of:
e: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure of village, block and district level institutions.

q: The only President of India who was elected unopposed is:
e: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy is the only President of India to have been elected unopposed, in the presidential election of 1977.

q: The first State in India to be formed on a linguistic basis, in 1953, was:
e: Andhra Pradesh, formed in 1953 out of the Telugu-speaking areas of Madras State, was the first State in India created on a linguistic basis.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of Local Self-Government' in India?
e: Lord Ripon is regarded as the Father of Local Self-Government in India for his 1882 resolution promoting local bodies.

q: 'Dyarchy' (dual government) in the provinces of British India was introduced by the:
e: Dyarchy, or dual government in the provinces, was introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, based on the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.

q: The Ghadar Party, founded in 1913 to work for India's freedom from abroad, was established at:
e: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 at San Francisco in the USA by Indian revolutionaries working abroad for India's freedom.

q: The Chittagong Armoury Raid of 1930 was led by:
e: The Chittagong Armoury Raid of April 1930, an attempt to seize the British armouries, was led by Surya Sen, popularly called Masterda.

q: The 'Forward Bloc', a political party founded in 1939, was established by:
e: The Forward Bloc was founded in 1939 by Subhas Chandra Bose after his resignation from the Congress presidency.

q: In the Battle of Hydaspes (326 BC), fought on the banks of the river Jhelum, Alexander the Great defeated the Indian king:
e: In the Battle of Hydaspes (326 BC), fought on the banks of the Jhelum, Alexander the Great defeated the Indian king Porus.

q: The First Buddhist Council, held shortly after the death of Gautama Buddha, was convened at:
e: The First Buddhist Council was convened at Rajgir (Rajagriha) shortly after the death of Gautama Buddha, to compile his teachings.

q: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 was enacted largely through the efforts of:
e: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 was enacted largely through the sustained efforts of the reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

q: The princely state of Hyderabad was merged into the Indian Union in 1948 through the police action known as:
e: Hyderabad was integrated into the Indian Union in September 1948 through the police action codenamed Operation Polo.

q: The river Kaveri (Cauvery) originates from:
e: The river Kaveri originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Karnataka and flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu to the Bay of Bengal.

q: The river Narmada originates from:
e: The Narmada originates from the Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward through a rift valley to the Gulf of Khambhat.

q: The southernmost point of the mainland of India is:
e: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) is the southernmost point of the Indian mainland; Indira Point in the Nicobar Islands is the southernmost point of India as a whole.

q: The 'Nine Degree Channel' of the Indian Ocean separates:

options.A: The Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands
options.C: Minicoy Island from the main group of the Lakshadweep Islands

e: The Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy Island from the main group of the Lakshadweep Islands.

q: Which region of India is popularly known as the 'Ruhr of India' for its rich mineral and industrial resources?
e: The Chota Nagpur Plateau is called the Ruhr of India because of its rich deposits of coal and minerals and its concentration of heavy industries.

q: The first Biosphere Reserve established in India (1986) was the:
e: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, established in 1986 across Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, was the first biosphere reserve of India.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Luni is a river of inland drainage which is lost in the Rann of Kutch.
2. The Periyar is the longest river of Kerala.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. The Luni is a river of inland drainage that is lost in the marshes of the Rann of Kutch, and the Periyar is the longest river of Kerala.

q: The black (regur) soil of the Deccan region is considered most suitable for the cultivation of:
e: Black (regur) soil, formed from Deccan lava and able to retain moisture, is most suitable for cotton cultivation.

q: Most of the rainfall received by the Coromandel coast, including Tamil Nadu, occurs during the season of the:
e: The Coromandel coast, including Tamil Nadu, receives most of its rainfall during the retreating or North-East monsoon in October to December.

q: The Suez Canal connects:

options.A: The Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean
options.B: The Black Sea and the Mediterranean Sea
options.C: The Persian Gulf and the Arabian Sea
options.D: The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea

e: The Suez Canal of Egypt connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea, providing the shortest sea route between Europe and Asia.

q: The first Chairman of the Finance Commission of India was:
e: K. C. Neogy was the first Chairman of the Finance Commission of India, constituted in 1951 under Article 280.

q: The 'Repo Rate' in the Indian banking system is the rate at which:

options.A: The Reserve Bank of India lends money to commercial banks
options.B: Commercial banks lend money to the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Commercial banks lend money to their customers
options.D: Banks lend money to each other overnight

e: The Repo Rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends money to commercial banks against securities.

q: The Gini coefficient is used in economics as a measure of:

options.A: The rate of inflation in an economy
options.B: Inequality in the distribution of income
options.C: The growth rate of national income

e: The Gini coefficient is a measure of inequality in the distribution of income or wealth in an economy, ranging from 0 (perfect equality) to 1.

q: The period of the 'Plan Holiday' in India's planned development, when annual plans replaced the Five-Year Plan, was:
e: The Plan Holiday period was 1966-69, when, after the Third Plan, annual plans were adopted instead of a Five-Year Plan before the Fourth Plan began.

q: The Sensex, the benchmark index of the Bombay Stock Exchange, is based on the share prices of how many blue-chip companies?
e: The Sensex, the benchmark index of the Bombay Stock Exchange, is based on the share prices of 30 financially sound blue-chip companies.

q: The neutron, one of the fundamental particles of the atom, was discovered by:
e: The neutron, the neutral particle of the atomic nucleus, was discovered by James Chadwick in 1932.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme'?

options.C: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam

e: Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha is regarded as the Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme and founded the atomic energy establishment in India.

q: The double-helix model of the structure of DNA was proposed by:

options.B: Gregor Mendel and Hugo de Vries

e: The double-helix model of DNA structure was proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953.

q: The smallest bone in the human body is the:
e: The stapes, located in the middle ear, is the smallest bone in the human body.

q: A 'Fathometer' is an instrument used for measuring:
e: A Fathometer is an instrument used for measuring the depth of the ocean, working on the principle of echo sounding.

q: The most abundant element in the Earth's crust is:
e: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust, accounting for nearly half of it by weight, followed by silicon.

q: The Minamata disease, which affected people in Japan, was caused by poisoning due to:
e: Minamata disease in Japan was caused by mercury poisoning, from industrial waste containing mercury compounds entering the food chain through fish.

q: The famous book 'An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations' (1776) was authored by:
e: 'The Wealth of Nations' (1776), the foundational work of modern economics, was authored by Adam Smith.

q: The first Indian feature film, 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913), was made by:
e: Raja Harishchandra (1913), India's first feature film, was made by Dadasaheb Phalke, honoured as the father of Indian cinema.

q: The first FIFA World Cup, held in 1930, was won by:
e: The first FIFA World Cup, held in 1930 in Uruguay, was won by the host country, Uruguay.

q: National Mathematics Day is celebrated in India every year on:
e: National Mathematics Day is celebrated on 22 December, the birth anniversary of the great mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan.

q: The first Indian woman to climb the summit of Mount Everest was:
e: Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest when she reached the summit in 1984.

q: The Chennai division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Chennai division, one of the oldest divisions, is a part of the Southern Railway headquartered at Chennai.

q: The Bengaluru division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Bengaluru division of Indian Railways is administered by the South Western Railway, whose headquarters is at Hubballi.

q: The Adra division is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Adra division in West Bengal is a part of the South Eastern Railway, headquartered at Garden Reach, Kolkata.

q: The Guntakal division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: Guntakal division now belongs to the South Coast Railway (HQ Visakhapatnam). (Source: Ministry of Railways Gazette notification dated 04.05.2026 constituting South Coast Railway, comprising Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions; operations from 01.06.2026.)

q: The Varanasi division is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Varanasi division is administered by the North Eastern Railway, whose headquarters is at Gorakhpur.

q: The Bhopal division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Bhopal division of Indian Railways is a part of the West Central Railway, headquartered at Jabalpur.

q: The Rajkot division belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Rajkot division in Saurashtra belongs to the Western Railway, headquartered at Churchgate, Mumbai.

q: The Sonpur division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Sonpur division in Bihar is administered by the East Central Railway, headquartered at Hajipur.

q: Nagpur is a divisional headquarters on two zonal railways. These two zones are:

options.B: Central Railway and South East Central Railway
options.C: South Eastern Railway and East Coast Railway
options.D: West Central Railway and South Central Railway

e: Nagpur is a divisional headquarters on two zones: the Central Railway and the South East Central Railway (headquartered at Bilaspur).

q: The Great Indian Peninsula Railway, which ran India's first train in 1853, later became the core of which zonal railway?
e: The Great Indian Peninsula Railway, which ran India's first train in 1853, later became the core of the Central Railway, formed in 1951.

q: The Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway (BB&CI), a major pre-Independence railway company, was the predecessor of which zonal railway?
e: The Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway (BB&CI) was the predecessor of the Western Railway, one of the oldest railway systems of India.

q: In terms of route length, the largest zonal railway of Indian Railways is the:
e: The Northern Railway, headquartered at New Delhi, is the largest zonal railway of India in terms of route length.

q: The South Central Railway, with headquarters at Secunderabad, was formed in the year:
e: The South Central Railway, with headquarters at Secunderabad, was formed in 1966 by carving out divisions from the Southern and Central Railways.

q: The Integral Coach Factory at Perambur was set up with technical collaboration from:
e: The Integral Coach Factory at Perambur, Chennai, was set up with technical collaboration from Switzerland for manufacturing modern passenger coaches.

q: The railway township of Chittaranjan, where the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works is located, is named after:
e: The railway township of Chittaranjan in West Bengal, home of the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works, is named after Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das.

q: The Mughalsarai Junction railway station in Uttar Pradesh was renamed as:
e: Mughalsarai Junction in Uttar Pradesh was renamed Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction in honour of the philosopher and political leader.

q: The historic Darjeeling Mail, one of the oldest trains of Eastern Railway, runs between Sealdah and:
e: The historic Darjeeling Mail of Eastern Railway runs between Sealdah (Kolkata) and New Jalpaiguri, the gateway to North Bengal and the North-East.

q: The Shivalik Deluxe Express, a popular tourist train of the hills, runs between:
e: The Shivalik Deluxe Express is a popular tourist train running on the UNESCO-listed Kalka-Shimla narrow gauge line between Kalka and Shimla.

q: The Himsagar Express, one of the longest-distance train services of India, connects Kanyakumari with:
e: The Himsagar Express, among India's longest-distance trains, connects Kanyakumari in the far south with Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra in Jammu and Kashmir.

q: The Falaknuma Express runs between:
e: The Falaknuma Express runs between Secunderabad and Howrah, taking its name from the Falaknuma Palace of Hyderabad.

q: The Udyan Express runs between:
e: The Udyan Express runs between Mumbai CSMT and KSR Bengaluru, serving passengers between Maharashtra and Karnataka.

q: The Azad Hind Express runs between:
e: The Azad Hind Express runs between Pune and Howrah, linking Maharashtra with West Bengal.

q: The Netravati Express runs between Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (Mumbai) and:
e: The Netravati Express runs between Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (Mumbai) and Thiruvananthapuram Central, travelling along the Konkan and Malabar coasts.

q: The Jhelum Express, a long-running train from the Pune side, runs between Pune and:
e: The Jhelum Express is a long-running daily train between Pune and Jammu Tawi, named after the river Jhelum.

q: The Maharashtra Express, running between Gondia and Kolhapur, is notable because it:

options.A: Is the fastest train of Maharashtra
options.B: Is the longest train of Indian Railways
options.D: Runs entirely within a single State

e: The Maharashtra Express, running between Gondia and Kolhapur, is notable for running entirely within a single State, Maharashtra.

q: The Pandian, Cholan and Cheran Express trains of Southern Railway are named after:

options.C: Ancient ports of the Coromandel coast

e: The Pandian, Cholan and Cheran Express trains are named after the Pandya, Chola and Chera, the three ancient Tamil dynasties.

q: The Nellai Express, running between Chennai Egmore and Tirunelveli, takes its name from 'Nellai', which is the popular Tamil name of:
e: Nellai Express takes its name from 'Nellai', the popular Tamil name of Tirunelveli, to which it runs from Chennai Egmore.

q: The Sachkhand Express, running between Nanded and Amritsar, is named after:

options.A: Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib at Nanded

e: The Sachkhand Express is named after Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib at Nanded, one of the five Takhts of Sikhism; the train runs between Nanded and Amritsar.

q: The Hazarduari Express of Eastern Railway is named after:
e: The Hazarduari Express is named after the Hazarduari Palace at Murshidabad, famous for its hall of a thousand doors.

q: The Konark Express, running between Bhubaneswar and Mumbai, derives its name from:
e: The Konark Express derives its name from the Sun Temple at Konark in Odisha, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

q: In railway working, a 'slip coach' refers to a coach which is:

options.B: Attached to trains only during festivals
options.C: Detached at an intermediate station and attached to another train for a different destination
options.D: Used only for carrying railway mail

e: A slip coach is a coach detached at an intermediate station and attached to another train to reach a different destination, saving passengers a change of train.

q: A 'mixed train' on Indian Railways is a train which carries:

options.C: Passengers booked on two different trains

e: A mixed train carries both passengers and goods in the same train, a pattern once common on branch and narrow gauge lines.

q: On broad gauge, a Mail/Express train is classified as a 'Superfast' train if its average speed, including halts, is not less than:
e: On broad gauge, a Mail/Express train is classified as Superfast if its average speed, including halts, is not less than 55 km per hour.

q: In a goods train, the brake van provided at the rear end is primarily meant for:

options.B: The guard, who travels in it and can apply brakes in an emergency
options.C: Carrying the train's tools and equipment

e: The brake van at the rear of a goods train is meant for the guard, who travels in it and can apply the brakes in an emergency.

q: The Vigilance Control Device (VCD) provided in locomotives is a safety device which:

options.A: Keeps the loco pilot alert by requiring periodic responses, failing which penalty brakes are applied
options.B: Records the speed of the train
options.C: Controls the train automatically at signals
options.D: Monitors the fuel level of the locomotive

e: The Vigilance Control Device keeps the loco pilot alert by requiring periodic responses; if the pilot fails to respond, penalty brakes are applied automatically.

q: In railway safety terminology, 'SPAD', considered a serious occurrence, stands for:
e: SPAD stands for Signal Passing At Danger, that is, a train passing a signal at danger without authority, a serious safety occurrence.

q: In railway engineering, the term 'P-Way' refers to the:

options.B: Points and crossings of a yard
options.D: Permanent Way, i.e., the track structure of rails, sleepers and ballast

e: P-Way stands for Permanent Way, the track structure itself, comprising rails, sleepers, ballast and fittings.

q: The 'BTPN' wagons of Indian Railways are bogie tank wagons used mainly for carrying:
e: BTPN wagons are bogie tank wagons used mainly for carrying petroleum products such as petrol and diesel.

q: The first 'Ladies Special' suburban train service in India was introduced in 1992 on the suburban network of:
e: India's first Ladies Special suburban train was introduced in 1992 on the Mumbai suburban network, for the exclusive use of women passengers.

q: The 'UMID' initiative of Indian Railways, which provides a smart health card to railway employees, pensioners and their dependants, stands for:
e: UMID stands for Unique Medical Identification, the Indian Railways initiative that issues a smart health card to employees, pensioners and their dependants.
